title: 돌발 주제 모음
intro: 돌발 주제는 Background Survey에서 고르지 않은 날씨·교통·재활용·휴대폰·인터넷·명절·가구·은행 같은 일상 소재가 갑자기 나오는 문제입니다. 처음 듣는 주제라도 당황하지 말고 '서울에서 혼자 사는 IT 회사 마케팅팀 직장인'이라는 내 페르소나로 끌어오면 됩니다. 출근 지하철, 7층 아파트, 한강 조깅, 대전 본가처럼 이미 준비한 이야기를 재활용하면 어떤 돌발 질문에도 1분 이상 말할 수 있습니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장('Oh, ~? Let me think.') → 기본 정보(한국은/서울은 보통 ~) → 내 일상·세부(혼자 사는 직장인인 나는 ~) → 느낌·이유 → 마무리 문장('Yeah, that's ~.')
모르는 주제일수록 '나'의 이야기로 바로 연결하세요. 일반론 2문장 + 내 출퇴근·집·주말 이야기 4~5문장이면 충분합니다.
생각할 시간이 필요하면 'That's a good question.' / 'Let me think for a second.' 로 자연스럽게 시간을 버세요.
경험형(명절, 은행 문제)은 언제 → 무슨 일 → 내가 한 행동 → 결과·느낀 점 순서로 과거시제를 지키면 됩니다.

expressions.en: Oh, the weather? Let me think.
expressions.note: 돌발 주제 만능 시작 문장. 주제 단어만 바꾸기
어떤 주제든 내 페르소나로 연결하는 문장

expressions.en: I take the subway to work every day.
I use it almost every day.
These days, it's hard to imagine life without ~.
Back when I was in middle school, ~.
It's a lot more ~ than it used to be.
It's one of those things you don't appreciate until it's gone.
expressions.ko: 없어져 봐야 소중함을 아는 것 중 하나예요.
expressions.note: 휴대폰·은행 앱·가구 등에 두루 쓰는 감정 표현

expressions.en: I can't stress enough how ~ it is.
expressions.ko: 그게 얼마나 ~한지 아무리 강조해도 지나치지 않아요.

questions.en: Tell me about the weather in your country. What are the seasons like, and which season do you like the most?
questions.ko: 당신 나라의 날씨에 대해 말해 주세요. 계절은 어떤가요? 어떤 계절을 가장 좋아하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, the weather in Korea? Let me think.' → 사계절 기본 정보(여름 덥고 습함·장마, 겨울 추움) → 내가 좋아하는 계절(가을 — 한강 조깅) → 이유 → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
계절마다 형용사 하나씩(hot and humid, freezing, warm, cool)만 붙여도 IM3 답이 됩니다.
IH 이상은 '혼자 살아서 여름엔 에어컨 전기요금이 걱정'처럼 내 생활과 연결한 디테일을 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, the weather in Korea? Let me think. Korea has four seasons. Spring is warm, and there are a lot of cherry blossoms. Summer is really hot and humid, and it rains a lot in July. Winter is very cold and dry. I don't like it much. My favorite season is fall. The weather is cool and sunny, so I love jogging along the Han River after work. Yeah, that's the weather in Korea.
answers.IH: Oh, the weather in Korea? Sure, let me think. Korea has four clear seasons. Spring is warm and beautiful, and there are cherry blossoms everywhere, but there's also a lot of fine dust. Summer is really hot and humid, and we have a rainy season in July. Since I live alone, I worry about my electric bill because I use the air conditioner a lot. Winter is freezing and dry, so I don't go out much. My favorite season is definitely fall. The sky is clear, and the air is cool. I go jogging along the Han River three times a week, and in fall it's just perfect. The trees turn red and yellow, and the view is amazing. It really helps me relax after a busy day. Yeah, that's why I like fall the most.
answers.AL: Oh, the weather in Korea? That's a good question. Well, Korea has four pretty distinct seasons, and each one has its own charm. Spring is warm and lovely, and the whole city turns pink with cherry blossoms, although the fine dust can be really annoying some days. Summer, on the other hand, is brutally hot and humid, and we get a long rainy season in July. Since I live alone, I'm always a little nervous about my electric bill, because my air conditioner basically runs all night. Winter is freezing and dry, so on weekends I mostly stay in, wrap myself in a blanket and watch movies. But if I had to pick one, I'd say fall is hands down my favorite. The sky is so clear and blue, and the air is cool and crisp. I usually go jogging along the Han River three times a week after work, and in the fall it's just the best. The trees turn red and yellow, and watching the sunset over the river really helps me forget about my stressful day at the office. So yeah, that's pretty much the weather in Korea, and that's why fall is my favorite season.

questions.en: How do you usually get around in your city? Tell me about the public transportation you use and what a typical trip is like.
questions.ko: 당신은 도시에서 보통 어떻게 이동하나요? 이용하는 대중교통과 평소 이동 과정에 대해 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, how I get around? Let me tell you.' → 서울 대중교통 기본 정보(지하철·버스, 교통카드) → 내 출근길(지하철역 5분, 15분, 이어폰으로 음악) → 기타 이동(따릉이로 한강, KTX로 대전) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
First / Then / After that 으로 출근 과정을 순서대로 말하면 routine 질문에 딱 맞습니다.
IH 이상은 출근 시간 지옥철 같은 단점도 하나 넣어 균형을 맞추세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, how I get around? Let me tell you. I live in Seoul, and the public transportation here is really good. I usually take the subway. Every morning, I walk to the subway station near my apartment. It takes about five minutes. Then I take the subway to my office. It only takes fifteen minutes. I listen to music on the way. The subway is cheap and fast, but it's really crowded in the morning. Yeah, that's how I get around.
answers.IH: Oh, how I get around the city? Sure, let me tell you. I live in Seoul, and the public transportation here is really convenient. There are subways and buses everywhere, and you can use one card for both. I usually take the subway. Every morning, I leave my apartment around eight thirty and walk to the station. It's only five minutes away. Then I take the subway to my office, and it takes about fifteen minutes. I always put in my earphones and listen to K-pop on the way. The only bad thing is that the subway is super crowded during rush hour. On weekends, I sometimes ride a public bike to the Han River. And when I visit my family in Daejeon, I take the KTX. Yeah, that's how I usually get around.
answers.AL: Oh, how I get around the city? Sure, that's an easy one for me. I live in Seoul, and honestly, I can't stress enough how convenient the public transportation is here. There are subway lines and buses going pretty much everywhere, and you just tap one card for all of them, so I've never really felt the need to buy a car. My typical trip is my morning commute. I leave my apartment around eight thirty and walk about five minutes to the subway station. Then I hop on the train, and I'm at my office in just fifteen minutes. I always put in my earphones and listen to some IU songs, which helps me wake up and get ready for a long day of meetings. The one thing I can't stand, though, is rush hour. The trains are so packed that sometimes I can barely move, and it can be pretty exhausting. On weekends, I like to rent one of the city's public bikes and ride to the Han River, which takes about ten minutes. And when I go down to see my family in Daejeon, I take the KTX, which is fast and comfortable. So yeah, that's pretty much how I get around.

questions.en: Tell me about recycling in your country. How does it work, and what do you do at home to recycle?
questions.ko: 당신 나라의 재활용에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떻게 이루어지며, 집에서 재활용을 위해 무엇을 하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, recycling in Korea? Let me think.' → 기본 정보(종류별 분리: 플라스틱·캔·종이·음식물) → 우리 아파트 방식(1층 분리수거장, 정해진 요일) → 혼자 사는 나의 습관(배달 용기 씻기) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
plastic, cans, paper, glass, food waste 다섯 단어만 알아도 기본 설명이 됩니다.
IH 이상은 '혼자 살아서 배달 음식 용기가 많이 나온다'는 솔직한 디테일로 진정성을 더하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, recycling in Korea? Let me think. In Korea, people recycle a lot. We separate plastic, cans, paper and glass. Food waste goes in a special bag. In my apartment building, there is a recycling area on the first floor. I live alone, so I don't have a lot of trash. But I order delivery food sometimes, so I wash the plastic containers. I take out my recycling every Sunday night. Yeah, that's how recycling works.
answers.IH: Oh, recycling in Korea? Sure, let me think. Recycling is really important in Korea, and the rules are pretty strict. People separate their trash into plastic, cans, paper, glass and food waste. You also have to buy special trash bags for general garbage. In my apartment building, there's a recycling area on the first floor, and we can only use it on certain days. I live alone, so I don't make a lot of trash. But to be honest, I order delivery food a lot after work, so I get many plastic containers. I always wash them and take off the labels before I throw them out. Every Sunday night, I take everything down from the seventh floor. It's a little annoying, but it makes me feel good. Yeah, that's pretty much how recycling works here.
answers.AL: Oh, recycling in Korea? That's a good question. Well, Korea takes recycling really seriously, and the rules are a lot stricter than in many other countries. Basically, you have to sort your trash into plastic, cans, paper, glass and food waste, and for regular garbage you need to buy special bags from the convenience store. If you don't follow the rules, you can actually get fined. In my apartment building, there's a recycling area on the first floor, and we're only allowed to use it on certain days of the week. Since I live alone, I don't produce that much trash, but I have to admit I order delivery food a lot, especially after a long day at work. So I end up with a mountain of plastic containers. I always rinse them out and peel off the labels, which is kind of a pain, but I know it really helps. Every Sunday night, I carry everything down from the seventh floor, and it's become a little routine for me. Actually, after doing this for three years, I've started to cook at home more just to cut down on waste. So yeah, that's pretty much how recycling works in Korea.

questions.en: How has the way people use phones changed over the years? How is it different from when you were younger?
questions.ko: 사람들이 휴대폰을 쓰는 방식은 그동안 어떻게 바뀌었나요? 당신이 어렸을 때와 어떻게 다른가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, how phones have changed? Let me think.' → 과거(중학생 때 폴더폰, 문자·전화만) → 현재(스마트폰으로 업무 메신저·은행·넷플릭스) → 내 생각(편하지만 너무 의존) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
used to + 동사원형(과거 습관) 과 These days / Now 를 대비시키는 것이 비교 질문의 핵심입니다.
IH 이상은 '퇴근 후에도 업무 메시지가 와서 쉬기 어렵다'처럼 직장인 관점의 단점을 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, how phones have changed? Let me think. When I was in middle school, I had a flip phone. I only used it to call my parents and send text messages. Now everyone has a smartphone. I use my phone for everything. I check my work messages, watch Netflix on the subway and use banking apps. It's really convenient. But I think I use it too much. Yeah, that's how phones have changed.
answers.IH: Oh, how phones have changed over the years? Sure, let me think. When I was in middle school, I had a small flip phone. Back then, I only used it to call my parents or text my friends. Texting was expensive, so I tried to keep my messages short. These days, it's hard to imagine life without a smartphone. I use my phone for almost everything. I check my work messenger, pay for things, do my banking and watch Netflix on the subway. It's a lot more convenient than it used to be. But there's a downside too. Even after work, my team sometimes sends me messages, so it's hard to really relax. Also, people look at their phones all the time instead of talking. Yeah, that's how phones have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, how the way people use phones has changed? That's a good question. Back when I was in middle school, I had a tiny pink flip phone, and I only used it to call my parents or text my friends. Texting actually cost money back then, so I used to squeeze everything into really short messages. These days, it's hard to imagine life without a smartphone. It's basically a computer in your pocket. I use mine for pretty much everything, from checking our team messenger and joining video calls to paying for coffee, doing my banking and watching Netflix on the subway. Since I work in marketing, I also check social media all day to keep up with the latest trends. So in a lot of ways, life has become much more convenient. But honestly, there's a dark side too. Because my phone is always with me, work never really ends, and I sometimes get messages from my team late at night. On top of that, when I meet my friends, everyone keeps checking their phones instead of actually talking. So these days I try to put my phone away at dinner. Yeah, that's pretty much how phones have changed.

questions.en: What do you usually do on the internet? Tell me about the websites or apps you use most and when you use them.
questions.ko: 인터넷으로 보통 무엇을 하나요? 가장 많이 쓰는 웹사이트나 앱과, 언제 쓰는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, what I do online? Let me tell you.' → 회사에서(SNS 트렌드 조사, 메일·메신저) → 출퇴근길(음악 스트리밍, 유튜브) → 집에서(넷플릭스, 온라인 쇼핑) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
In the morning / At work / After work 처럼 시간대별로 나누면 routine 질문이 깔끔하게 정리됩니다.
IH 이상은 '마케팅팀이라 인스타그램을 일로도 본다'는 페르소나 디테일로 차별화하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, what I do on the internet? Let me tell you. I use the internet all day. At work, I check emails and look at Instagram for my marketing job. On the subway, I listen to music on a streaming app. After work, I watch YouTube or Netflix at home. I also shop online a lot, because I live alone and I'm busy. It's really convenient. Yeah, that's what I usually do on the internet.
answers.IH: Oh, what I do on the internet? Sure, let me tell you. Honestly, I'm online almost all day. In the morning, I listen to K-pop on a music streaming app on the subway. At work, I'm on the marketing team, so I use the internet a lot for my job. I check emails, use our team messenger and look at Instagram to see what's trending. After work, I usually relax by watching YouTube videos or a movie on Netflix. On Friday nights, I watch movies for hours. I also do a lot of online shopping, because I live alone and don't have much time. I even buy groceries online, and they come the next morning. It saves me a lot of time. Yeah, that's pretty much what I do on the internet.
answers.AL: Oh, what I usually do on the internet? Well, to be honest, I'm pretty much online from the moment I wake up until I go to bed. In the morning, I put on a music streaming app and listen to my IU playlist on the subway. Once I get to the office, the internet basically is my job. Since I'm on the marketing team at an IT company, I spend a lot of time on Instagram and YouTube, checking out what's trending and what our competitors are posting. Of course, I'm also constantly answering emails and messages from my team. After work, I like to unwind with YouTube or Netflix, and on Friday nights I usually binge-watch a comedy or an action movie. I also do a ton of online shopping. Since I live alone and I'm always busy, I even order my groceries online, and they show up at my door early the next morning, which is a total lifesaver. The only problem is that I sometimes stay up way too late scrolling on my phone. So these days, I'm trying to put it down an hour before bed. Yeah, that's pretty much what I do online.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable holiday you celebrated, like Chuseok or New Year's. What did you do, who were you with, and why was it special?
questions.ko: 추석이나 설날처럼 기억에 남는 명절에 대해 말해 주세요. 무엇을 했고, 누구와 함께였고, 왜 특별했나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, a memorable holiday? Let me think.' → 언제(작년 추석) → 무엇을(KTX로 대전 본가, 엄마 음식, 남동생 Junho와 송편) → 왜 특별했는지(혼자 살아서 가족이 더 소중) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
과거시제를 지키고, 장소(Daejeon)·사람(my parents, Junho)·음식(songpyeon) 고유명사를 넣으면 생생해집니다.
AL은 '혼자 살다 보니 집밥이 그리웠다'는 감정으로 특별한 이유를 깊게 말하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a memorable holiday? Let me think. Last Chuseok, I visited my family in Daejeon. I live alone in Seoul, so I don't see them often. I took the KTX, and it was really crowded. My mom made a lot of delicious food. My younger brother Junho and I made songpyeon together. We also watched movies and talked a lot. It was so nice to be home. Yeah, that's my most memorable holiday.
answers.IH: Oh, a memorable holiday? Sure, let me think. I think last Chuseok was really special. I live alone in Seoul, and I'm always busy with work, so I don't get to see my family very often. So I took a few extra days off and went down to Daejeon on the KTX. The train was packed, but I was so excited. When I got home, my mom had already made tons of food, like japchae and pancakes. My younger brother Junho and I made songpyeon together, and his were really ugly, so we laughed a lot. At night, we all watched a comedy movie in the living room. It felt just like when I was a kid. I really missed my mom's cooking. Yeah, that's why last Chuseok was so special for me.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable holiday? Let me think for a second. I'd have to say last Chuseok was really special. Since I moved to Seoul for work three years ago, I've been living on my own, and with all the meetings and deadlines, I honestly don't get to see my family as much as I'd like. So last year, I took a couple of extra days off and headed down to Daejeon on the KTX. The train was absolutely packed with people carrying gift boxes, but I didn't mind at all because I was so excited. When I walked into my parents' apartment, the whole place smelled amazing. My mom had been cooking all morning, and the table was covered with japchae, pancakes and all my favorite dishes. My younger brother Junho and I made songpyeon together, and his came out so lumpy that we couldn't stop laughing. That night, the four of us watched a comedy movie in the living room, just like we used to when I was in school. Living alone, I'd kind of forgotten how warm that feels. It's one of those things you don't appreciate until it's gone. So yeah, that's why last Chuseok was so memorable for me.

questions.en: Tell me about your favorite piece of furniture in your home. What does it look like, where is it, and why do you like it?
questions.ko: 집에서 가장 좋아하는 가구에 대해 말해 주세요. 어떻게 생겼고, 어디에 있으며, 왜 좋아하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, my favorite piece of furniture? Let me think.' → 무엇(거실의 회색 소파) → 생김새·위치(TV 맞은편, 발코니 옆) → 이유(금요일 밤 영화, 퇴근 후 휴식) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
색깔·크기·재질(gray, soft, a two-seater) 형용사 3개만 넣어도 묘사가 풍성해집니다.
IH 이상은 '이사 올 때 처음 내 돈으로 산 가구'처럼 사연을 붙여 이유를 강화하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, my favorite piece of furniture? Let me think. I think it's my sofa. It's in my living room, right in front of the TV. It's gray, and it's really soft and comfortable. It's not very big, but it's perfect for me because I live alone. After work, I lie on the sofa and relax. On Friday nights, I watch movies on it. Yeah, that's my favorite piece of furniture.
answers.IH: Oh, my favorite piece of furniture? Sure, let me think. I'd say it's definitely my sofa. It's in my living room, right across from the TV and next to the balcony door. It's a light gray two-seater, and it's really soft. I also put a few cute cushions and a warm blanket on it. I bought it when I moved into this apartment three years ago. It was the first expensive thing I bought with my own salary, so it means a lot to me. After a long day of meetings, I just lie down on it and listen to music. And every Friday night, I sit there with some snacks and watch Netflix. Sometimes I even fall asleep on it. It's my favorite spot in the whole apartment. Yeah, that's why I love my sofa.
answers.AL: Oh, my favorite piece of furniture? That's an easy one. It's definitely my sofa. It sits in my living room, right across from the TV and next to the door to my little balcony, so I can see my plants from there. It's a light gray two-seater, and it's so soft that you kind of sink into it. I've also covered it with a few cute cushions and a fluffy blanket, so it's super cozy. I actually bought it when I moved into this apartment three years ago, right after I started working. It was the first really expensive thing I ever bought with my own salary, so it means a lot more to me than just a place to sit. These days, it's pretty much the center of my life at home. After a long, stressful day of meetings, I just collapse onto it and put on some ballads. And every Friday night, I curl up there with a bag of chips and binge-watch movies on Netflix. To be honest, I fall asleep on it more often than I'd like to admit. Living alone, it's kind of my little safe place. So yeah, that's why my sofa is my favorite piece of furniture.

questions.en: Have you ever had a problem at a bank or with a banking app? Tell me what happened and how you solved it.
questions.ko: 은행이나 은행 앱에서 문제가 생긴 적이 있나요? 무슨 일이 있었고 어떻게 해결했는지 말해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, a problem with a bank? Let me think.' → 언제(작년, 휴대폰을 바꾼 뒤) → 문제(비밀번호 오류로 은행 앱 잠김, 친구에게 돈을 못 보냄) → 해결(점심시간에 신분증 들고 회사 근처 지점 방문) → 'Yeah, that's ~.'
문제 상황 → 내 행동 → 결과의 3단계를 과거시제로 지키세요.
IH 이상은 '은행이 6시에 닫아서 점심시간밖에 갈 수 없었다'처럼 직장인다운 어려움을 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a problem with a bank? Let me think. Last year, I got a new phone and downloaded my banking app again. But I forgot my password. I tried too many times, and the app got locked. I couldn't send money to my friend for dinner. So I went to a bank near my office during lunch. I showed my ID, and they fixed it. Yeah, that's how I solved the problem.
answers.IH: Oh, a problem with a bank? Sure, let me think. Last year, I got a new phone, so I had to set up my banking app again. But I couldn't remember my password. I tried a few times, and then the app got locked. That was a big problem, because I had to send money to my friends for a dinner we had. I called the bank, but they said I had to visit a branch with my ID. The problem was that banks close at four, and I work until six. So I went to a branch near my office during my lunch break. I had to wait for almost thirty minutes, so I couldn't eat lunch. But they unlocked my account quickly. Yeah, that's how I solved the problem.
answers.AL: Oh, a problem with a banking app? Actually, yes, I've had one. Last year, I finally upgraded to a new phone, so I had to set up my banking app all over again. The problem was that I couldn't remember my password at all, because I'd been using my fingerprint for years. I tried a few different passwords, and after the fifth try, the app just locked me out. That was a real headache, because my friends and I had just had a big dinner together, and I was supposed to send them my share that night. I called the bank's customer center, and they told me I had to visit a branch in person with my ID. But here's the thing. Banks in Korea close at four, and I work until six, so it was almost impossible. In the end, I rushed to a branch near my office during my lunch break. There was a long line, and I had to wait for about thirty minutes, so I ended up skipping lunch. But the staff were really kind, and they unlocked my account in just a few minutes. Since then, I've written my password down in a safe place. So yeah, that's how I solved my banking problem.

patterns.en: When it comes to seasons, I'm a huge fan of fall.
patterns.ko: 계절로 말하자면, 저는 가을을 정말 좋아해요.

patterns.en: It's only a five-minute walk from my house to the subway station.
It's not very big, but it's perfect for me because I live alone.
patterns.ko: 아주 크진 않지만, 혼자 사는 저한테는 딱 좋아요.

patterns.en: First, I listen to K-pop on the subway. Then, I check emails and Instagram trends at work.
patterns.ko: 먼저 지하철에서 K-pop을 들어요. 그다음 회사에서 이메일과 인스타그램 트렌드를 확인해요.

patterns.en: Whenever I take out my recycling on Sunday night, I feel good about protecting the environment.
patterns.ko: 일요일 밤에 분리수거를 내놓을 때마다 환경을 지키는 것 같아 기분이 좋아요.

patterns.en: I'll never forget last Chuseok because my brother Junho and I laughed so much while making songpyeon.
patterns.ko: 남동생 준호와 송편을 빚으며 정말 많이 웃어서 작년 추석은 절대 못 잊을 거예요.

patterns.en: I had a problem with my banking app after I got a new phone.
patterns.ko: 새 휴대폰으로 바꾼 뒤 은행 앱에 문제가 생겼어요.

patterns.en: I used to only call my parents and text my friends on my flip phone, but now I use my smartphone for almost everything.
patterns.ko: 예전에는 폴더폰으로 부모님께 전화하고 친구들에게 문자만 했지만, 지금은 스마트폰으로 거의 모든 걸 해요.
